newsitem.title: UK: BOE says City bonus levels of increasing concern.
newsitem.headline: BOE says City bonus levels of increasing concern.

text.p: The salary and bonus policies of firms in the financial markets are an increasing concern to regulators as they play a large part in overall risk management strategy, the Bank of England said on Monday.
In its latest Financial Stability Review, the Bank said firms must take care not encourage bad behaviour.
"If large bonuses are paid to employees who make money but are perceived to have a cavalier attitude to compliance, it is likely to encourage similar behaviour in others," the Bank said.
If this were to happen, the result would be that unnecessary strain is put on a firm's other management and control systems.
The article also looked at the effects of remuneration on a financial business from the costs point of view.

The rationale behind paying high levels of performance-related bonuses in comparison to salary is that costs can then be closely linked to revenues and this reduces the danger volatility in the income stream.
But the need to keep employees, often a firm's most precious 'asset', means that the ability to change remuneration is often more apparent than real, the Bank argued.
It warned that managements of financial sector firms must recognise the proportion of costs that are actually fixed or variable when assessing the quality of an income stream
